preheader: Tesla to halt Cybertruck production, Circle hits $13.9T volume, and Rioux debuts for UCI.

lead.headline: Tesla to End Cybertruck Production and Refund Select Deposits
lead.body: Elon Musk announced that Tesla will end Cybertruck production in about eight months, defending the decision by stating order volume outpaced output capacity. Tesla will also issue refunds for certain reservation deposits as it winds down the vehicle line.
lead.why: It shows the reality of high-cost product manufacturing. Even high-profile products get cut when unit costs, production headaches, and actual margins fail to align.

stories.headline: Circle Reports 17% Revenue Rise as USDC Volume Hits $13.9T
stories.body: Circle Internet Group posted Q3 revenue of $865 million, up 17% year over year. Total on-chain transaction volume for its USDC stablecoin jumped 49% to $13.9 trillion.
stories.why: As a business major, this gives you a clear window into how digital currency firms make money through reserve yields and transaction volume.

stories.headline: NASA Unveils $10 Billion in Moon Base Cargo Contracts
stories.body: NASA awarded up to $10 billion in commercial contracts to ferry cargo to the moon as it works toward establishing a crewed base by 2032. The program also features plans for a nuclear-powered rover.
stories.why: Federal procurement programs of this size create massive multi-year budgets for commercial aerospace contractors and specialized engineering startups.

stories.headline: North Korea Mints Meme Coins to Launder $6.4 Billion Binance Hack
stories.body: Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic discovered that North Korean hackers are issuing worthless meme tokens and setting up trading pools on Tron, NEAR, and Solana. The setup lets them wash funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers.
stories.why: If you look into fintech or crypto venture investing, understanding these laundering routes shows where regulators will place compliance pressure next.

stories.headline: SBI Report Finds Global AI Capex Pauses Could Shift Capital to India
stories.body: A report from SBI Funds indicates that global investors are questioning the fast pace of artificial intelligence capital expenditures. That caution is prompting funds to rotate into Indian equities.
stories.why: Tracking how asset managers rotate money when a major tech spending cycle cools off is core preparation for finance and markets interviews.

stories.headline: Bain Capital's Ajay Agarwal Points to Growth in Physical AI
stories.body: Ajay Agarwal, an early backer of Kiva Systems before its $775 million sale to Amazon, argued that robotics is entering its strongest cycle yet. He noted that merging AI software with physical hardware is opening high-conviction venture bets.
stories.why: This shows how top venture capitalists spot long-term hardware and software cycles, which is useful context if you aim for venture capital or startup operations.

stories.headline: BirlaNu Enlists BCG for Operational Turnaround at Parador
stories.body: Indian firm BirlaNu reported its quarterly earnings and highlighted an ongoing Boston Consulting Group operational restructuring. The BCG initiative identified between 9 million and 14 million euros in potential operating profit gains for BirlaNu's Parador unit.
stories.why: This is a real-world example of management consulting deliverables, specifically showing how firms quantify operational improvements for struggling corporate units.

stories.headline: 7-Foot-9 Center Olivier Rioux Debuts with Double-Double for UCI
stories.body: Olivier Rioux, the tallest player in college basketball history, made his UC Irvine debut on Tuesday night. He put up 13 points and 12 rebounds in 18 minutes to help the Anteaters defeat Chapman 92-66.

stories.headline: Carlos Alcaraz Outlasts Ben Shelton to Take Paris Masters
stories.body: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Ben Shelton 7-6(5), 7-5 in the Paris Masters final. The victory marks Alcaraz's fifth title of 2026 and the 29th tournament crown of his career.

term.name: Liquidity Pool
term.definition: A digital pot of cryptocurrency tokens locked in a smart contract that allows traders to swap tokens automatically without waiting for an individual buyer or seller. Instead of using a traditional exchange order book, trades happen against the pool's assets. Today, Elliptic reported that North Korean hackers created their own pools to swap stolen funds into clean tokens.

serve.headline: Crowd Threat raised £1M to crowdsource physical threat intelligence
serve.body: Crowd Threat, launched by a former British Army intelligence operator, combines local eyewitness incident reports with AI analysis to flag security threats faster than remote teams can. The startup raised 1 million pounds in seed funding to expand its reporting platform.

How can an AI filter prevent bad actors from submitting fake reports to cause false alarms?
Could a neighborhood-level intelligence feed be adapted into an alert product for university campuses like UC Irvine?
